code.title: Overloaded Area Switchboard
code.description:
A geometry tool exposes one function name area() that behaves differently for squares and circles. Class AreaTool overloads area(int side) for squares and area(double radius) for circles. Read the shape code and value, then let the overload pick the right formula.

Input Format:
One line with a character and a number: 'S' with an integer side, or 'C' with a radius.

Output Format:
Square area: <side * side>
or
Circle area: <3.14 * radius * radius with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
Code is 'S' or 'C'; 1 <= value <= 100.
code.output1: Circle area: 3.14
code.output2: Square area: 144
code.output3: Circle area: 314.00
code.sampleoutput1: Square area: 25
code.sampleoutput2: Circle area: 12.56

code.title: Shape vs Circle Describe Drill
code.description:
Practice plain method overriding. Base class Shape has describe() printing 'I am a shape'. Derived class Circle redefines describe() to print 'I am a circle'. Read the picker and an item number, create the matching object directly, and call describe() on it.

Input Format:
One line with a character and an integer: the picker and the item number. 'C' creates a Circle; any other character creates a Shape.

Output Format:
Item <id>:
I am a circle   (when picker is C)
or
I am a shape    (otherwise)

Constraints:
1 <= item number <= 999.

Item 5:
I am a shape

code.title: Virtual Speak Through Base Pointer
code.description:
A virtual function lets a base class pointer call the derived class version. Animal declares speak() as virtual; Dog overrides it to bark. Read the dog's name, build a Dog, point a base Animal pointer at it, and call speak() through the pointer.

Input Format:
One line with a single word: the dog's name.

Output Format:
<name> says Woof Woof

Constraints:
Name is one word of at most 20 letters.

mcqs.title: Meaning of Polymorphism
mcqs.description: What does polymorphism mean in object-oriented programming?
mcqs.Option2: One name, many forms - the same interface behaving differently in different contexts
mcqs.Option3: Hiding data members inside a class
mcqs.Option4: Copying one object into another object

mcqs.title: Feature Behind Compile-Time Polymorphism
mcqs.description: Which C++ feature provides compile-time (static) polymorphism?

mcqs.title: Keyword for Virtual Dispatch
mcqs.description: Which keyword, used in the base class declaration, enables runtime (dynamic) dispatch of a method?

mcqs.title: What Function Overriding Means
mcqs.description: What is function overriding in C++?
mcqs.Option1: Two functions with the same name but different parameter lists in one class
mcqs.Option2: Redefining a base class method in a derived class with the same signature
mcqs.Option3: Calling a function before it has been declared
mcqs.Option4: Passing a function as an argument to another function

mcqs.title: Overriding Versus Overloading
mcqs.description: Which statement correctly distinguishes overriding from overloading?
mcqs.Option1: Overloading happens at runtime while overriding happens at compile time
mcqs.Option2: Overriding needs different parameter lists while overloading needs the same signature
mcqs.Option3: Overloading only works through base class pointers
mcqs.Option4: Overloading is the same name with different signatures in one scope; overriding is the same signature redefined in a derived class

mcqs.title: Purpose of a Virtual Function
mcqs.description: What is the main purpose of declaring a function virtual in the base class?
mcqs.Option1: To let a base pointer or reference pick the derived class version at runtime
mcqs.Option2: To make the function execute faster
mcqs.Option3: To allow the function to be called without any object
mcqs.Option4: To stop the function from being inherited

mcqs.title: Base Pointer Virtual Call Result
mcqs.description: A base class pointer stores the address of a derived object and calls a virtual method. Which version of the method runs?
mcqs.Option4: It depends on the pointer's declared type

mcqs.title: When Overloads Are Resolved
mcqs.description: When is the choice among overloaded functions (compile-time polymorphism) made?
mcqs.Option2: At compile time, based on the argument list

mcqs.title: True Statement About Virtual Functions
mcqs.description: Which statement about virtual functions is true?
mcqs.Option1: A virtual function must be declared static
mcqs.Option2: A virtual function cannot be overridden in a derived class
mcqs.Option3: Virtual functions can only be called with objects, never pointers
mcqs.Option4: Once a function is virtual in the base class, its overrides in derived classes are virtual automatically

mcqs.title: Tools Behind Runtime Polymorphism
mcqs.description: Runtime polymorphism in C++ is achieved using:
mcqs.Option3: Virtual functions together with base class pointers or references

mcqs.title: Why the Base Method Must Be Virtual
mcqs.description: Through a base pointer to a derived object, a NON-virtual base method is called. What happens and why?
mcqs.Option1: The derived version runs because the actual object is derived
